outcome.outcome: Intracellular molecular state becomes observable without perturbing the process being observed, making dynamic biochemistry measurable in living cells rather than inferred from fixed ones.
outcome.rationale: Their framing is that probes both fail to enter and perturb what they measure; removing both makes in-situ dynamics readable.

ai_types.rationale: Both listed capabilities are design problems: engineering label-free contrast and metabolically incorporable reporters.
Label-free modalities are signal-starved by construction, and learned reconstruction already recovers usable contrast.

measurability.rationale: Species resolved per cell, perturbation magnitude and time to phototoxicity are standard reported instrument metrics.

outcome.outcome: Whether quantum coherence plays a functional role in biology becomes an experimentally settled question rather than a standing theoretical dispute.
outcome.rationale: Their description is explicit that predictions exist and direct evidence does not; the unlock is adjudication.

ai_types.rationale: The blocker is extracting a coherence signature from a warm, wet, fast-dephasing system, which is a signal-recovery problem.

measurability.rationale: Candidate observables exist and have been measured, notably long-lived coherences in photosynthetic complexes, but the field disputes whether they are functional or artifacts of the spectroscopy, so measurement does not settle the question.

outcome.outcome: Disordered and allosteric proteins become predictable from sequence, extending structure-based design to the large fraction of the proteome that AlphaFold-class tools currently cannot represent.
outcome.rationale: Their description names the boundary precisely: stable proteins solved, dynamic ones not.

ai_types.rationale: This is the same learned-prediction problem as static structure, retargeted at conformational ensembles rather than single structures.
NMR ensemble mapping supplies the training and validation labels the prediction problem lacks.

measurability.rationale: Ensemble prediction is scorable against NMR and SAXS observables, and CASP-style blind assessment already exists for the static case.

outcome.outcome: Optical imaging reaches depths that currently require removing or sectioning the tissue, making neural activity and diagnostic imaging observable in intact organisms.
outcome.rationale: Their description names deep-tissue neural mapping and noninvasive diagnostics as the two downstream unlocks.

ai_types.rationale: Scattering is an inverse problem; computational descattering and wavefront shaping are learned-estimation approaches with working prototypes.

measurability.rationale: Imaging depth in millimetres at a stated resolution and wavelength is the field's standard benchmark.

outcome.outcome: The same living cell can be imaged at nanoscale repeatedly, making longitudinal subcellular dynamics directly observable instead of reconstructed from fixed snapshots of different cells.
outcome.rationale: Their description names the loss precisely: destruction forecloses longitudinal study of one specimen.

ai_types.rationale: Destructiveness is a dose problem, and learned denoising and reconstruction directly reduce the dose needed for a given resolution.
Quantum electron microscopy and ghost imaging require instruments that do not yet exist outside proof-of-principle.

measurability.rationale: Resolution achieved against dose delivered against post-imaging viability is a three-way tradeoff that is routinely quantified.

outcome.outcome: Membrane proteins and small proteins become structurally tractable, opening the largest drug-target class and the hardest cryo-EM case to structure-based design.
outcome.rationale: Their description names both sub-cases; membrane proteins are the majority of drug targets, which is where the downstream unlock sits.

ai_types.rationale: Recoding membrane proteins for solubility is de novo sequence design, which works now for this class of objective.
Orientation assignment for small particles in cryo-EM is a learned inference problem already being attacked.

measurability.rationale: Structures deposited and resolution achieved below 50 kDa are directly countable in the PDB.

outcome.outcome: A formal, operational criterion separating living from nonliving matter becomes available, giving origin-of-life research and biosignature detection a testable target rather than a definitional argument.
outcome.rationale: Their description asks precisely for a framework precise enough to be practically useful, which is what biosignature work currently lacks.

ai_types.rationale: The listed capability is simulating nonequilibrium systems at scale, which is a surrogate-modelling problem far beyond current tractable system sizes.
Formal framework construction is theory work, where AI contribution remains unproven.

measurability.rationale: Candidate measures exist and are computed on real molecules, assembly theory and free-energy dissipation among them, but the field actively disputes whether any of them settles what life is. A measurement can be taken; the verdict is what is contested.

notes: Two tier-3 calls in this field, both on foundational rather than applied questions. Quantum biology is the cleanest verifier's-law case outside physics: the instrument exists, the interpretation is the blocker.
